about.title: From business to computer science,
intro: I'm Gary Alvarado, a Master's student in Computer Science at UC Davis. I started in Fall 2026 and expect to graduate in June 2028. I split my time between Davis and the Bay Area.

My bachelor's degree is in Business Administration from Cal State East Bay. I moved into tech through upper-division computer science coursework there, and found that what I enjoy most is building things people actually use, especially in education and health.
about.researchLead: I'm most interested in the places where these areas overlap, especially where AI and robotics meet human-computer interaction.

research.title: Computer vision
research.body: Teaching machines to understand images and movement, and using that to give people useful feedback.

research.title: Robotics
research.body: Systems that act in the physical world, and how people can work with them safely and naturally.

research.title: Human-computer interaction
research.body: Designing technology around the people who use it: clear, accessible, and actually helpful.

research.title: AI for education and health
research.body: Tools that help students learn difficult material and help people understand their bodies and health.

teaching: From September 2024 to July 2025 I was the long-term substitute for AP Computer Science Principles and Computer Programming in the Hayward Unified School District, teaching 130+ students across five sections. Several of my students passed the AP exam.
Teaching changed how I think about software. A good tool, like a good lesson, meets people where they are. That's why my projects lean toward study tools and clear interfaces.
about.teachingLink: See the showcase of 70+ student projects I built

experience.role: Long-term substitute teacher, AP Computer Science Principles and Computer Programming
points: Taught 130+ students across five sections, covering C++, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, networking, and data representation.
Designed hands-on projects and lessons that prepared students for the AP CS exam and built problem-solving skills.
Introduced students to industry tools, including GitHub and AI-assisted development.
Teach classes across grade levels and subjects, adapting to new classrooms and lesson plans every day.

services.title: Websites for small businesses
services.lead: I build fast, accessible websites that look good on every phone, in English, Spanish, or both. You get a site that's easy to update and fully yours.

offers.title: Landing pages
offers.body: A single, focused page for a launch, an event, or a new service, built to turn visitors into calls and messages.

offers.title: Small business websites
offers.body: A few pages that cover who you are, what you offer, where to find you, and how to reach you.

offers.title: Bilingual websites
offers.body: English and Spanish versions written to sound natural in each language, with a simple language switch.

offers.title: Redesigns
offers.body: A modern, mobile-friendly refresh of an existing site that keeps what works and fixes what doesn't.

included: Accessibility basics: readable contrast, keyboard navigation, alt text
Fast loading and basic search engine setup
A contact form that sends messages to your email
A short walkthrough so you can make simple updates

process.title: Call
process.body: We talk about your business, your customers, and what the site needs to do.

process.title: Design
process.body: I put together a layout and style for you to review before any building starts.

process.title: Build
process.body: I build the site, share a preview link, and make revisions based on your feedback.

process.title: Launch
process.body: We connect your domain, go live, and I show you how to keep things up to date.
